resource.name: aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream
resource.description: Provides a Kinesis Firehose Delivery Stream resource. Amazon Kinesis Firehose is a fully managed, elastic service to easily deliver real-time data streams to destinations such as Amazon S3 , Amazon Redshift and Snowflake. For more details, see the Amazon Kinesis Firehose Documentation.
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource enables the creation and management of Amazon Kinesis Firehose delivery streams for real-time data ingestion and delivery to destinations like Amazon S3, Amazon Redshift, and Snowflake. It is commonly used for building scalable data pipelines, integrating streaming data with storage and analytics platforms, and automating data delivery workflows. Users can configure source integrations (e.g., Kinesis Data Streams), destination settings, buffering, compression, encryption, and monitoring to optimize data flow and ensure secure, efficient processing.

examples.title: Extended S3 Destination

It showcases key configurations such as `dynamic_partitioning_configuration`, custom S3 prefixes for partitioning, and a `processing_configuration` block for transforming and enriching data streams.

examples.title: Redshift Destination
examples.code:
resource "aws_redshift_cluster" "test_cluster" {
  cluster_identifier = "tf-redshift-cluster"
  database_name      = "test"
  master_username    = "testuser"
  master_password    = "T3stPass"
  node_type          = "dc1.large"
  cluster_type       = "single-node"
}

resource "aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream" "test_stream" {
  name        = "terraform-kinesis-firehose-test-stream"
  destination = "redshift"

  redshift_configuration {
    role_arn           = aws_iam_role.firehose_role.arn
    cluster_jdbcurl    = "jdbc:redshift://${aws_redshift_cluster.test_cluster.endpoint}/${aws_redshift_cluster.test_cluster.database_name}"
    username           = "testuser"
    password           = "T3stPass"
    data_table_name    = "test-table"
    copy_options       = "delimiter '|'" # the default delimiter
    data_table_columns = "test-col"
    s3_backup_mode     = "Enabled"

    s3_configuration {
      role_arn           = aws_iam_role.firehose_role.arn
      bucket_arn         = aws_s3_bucket.bucket.arn
      buffering_size     = 10
      buffering_interval = 400
      compression_format = "GZIP"
    }

    s3_backup_configuration {
      role_arn           = aws_iam_role.firehose_role.arn
      bucket_arn         = aws_s3_bucket.bucket.arn
      buffering_size     = 15
      buffering_interval = 300
      compression_format = "GZIP"
    }
  }
}
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` with a Redshift destination, including the `redshift_configuration` block for JDBC connection, table settings, and `s3_backup_mode` for data backup. examples.title: Snowflake Destination
examples.code:
resource "aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream" "example_snowflake_destination" {
  name        = "example-snowflake-destination"
  destination = "snowflake"

  snowflake_configuration {
    account_url        = "https://example.snowflakecomputing.com"
    buffering_size     = 15
    buffering_interval = 600
    database           = "example-db"
    private_key        = "..."
    role_arn           = aws_iam_role.firehose.arn
    schema             = "example-schema"
    table              = "example-table"
    user               = "example-usr"

    s3_configuration {
      role_arn           = aws_iam_role.firehose.arn
      bucket_arn         = aws_s3_bucket.bucket.arn
      buffering_size     = 10
      buffering_interval = 400
      compression_format = "GZIP"
    }
  }
}
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` with a Snowflake destination, showcasing the `snowflake_configuration` block for integrating with a Snowflake database. It highlights key settings such as `account_url`, `private_key`, and `role_arn`, along with an embedded `s3_configuration` block for intermediate storage with GZIP compression, enabling efficient and secure data delivery to Snowflake.

arguments.name: arn
arguments.llm_summary: The `arn` argument for the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource represents the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the delivery stream, which uniquely identifies the stream within AWS. While not required, this argument is typically used for referencing the delivery stream in other resources, policies, or integrations, enabling users to establish dependencies, permissions, or cross-service interactions.

arguments.name: destination
arguments.description: – (Required) This is the destination to where the data is delivered. The only options are `s3` (Deprecated, use `extended_s3` instead), `extended_s3`, `redshift`, `elasticsearch`, `splunk`, `http_endpoint`, `opensearch`, `opensearchserverless` and `snowflake`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `destination` argument specifies the target service or storage location where data from the Kinesis Firehose delivery stream will be delivered, enabling users to define the integration point for their data pipeline. By setting this required argument, users can configure delivery to supported destinations such as S3, Redshift, Elasticsearch, Splunk, HTTP endpoints, OpenSearch, OpenSearch Serverless, or Snowflake, aligning the stream's output with their data processing, storage, or analytics goals.

arguments.name: destination_id
arguments.llm_summary: The `destination_id` argument for the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to specify a unique identifier for the delivery destination within the Firehose stream configuration. This enables precise targeting of a specific destination, such as an S3 bucket, Redshift table, or Elasticsearch domain, ensuring the stream's data is routed correctly to the intended endpoint for processing or storage.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument represents the unique identifier of the Kinesis Firehose delivery stream, typically auto-generated by AWS upon resource creation. While not user-configurable, it is useful for referencing the delivery stream in other resources or outputs, enabling integration and dependency management within your Terraform configuration.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: (Required) A name to identify the stream. This is unique to the AWS account and region the Stream is created in. When using for WAF logging, name must be prefixed with `aws-waf-logs-`. See AWS Documentation for more details.
arguments.llm_summary: The `name` argument specifies a unique identifier for the Kinesis Firehose delivery stream within the AWS account and region, enabling users to define and distinguish the stream for data delivery and processing. When used for WAF logging, it enforces a specific naming convention (`aws-waf-logs-` prefix) to ensure compatibility with AWS WAF log integration.

arguments.name: tags
arguments.description: (Optional) A map of tags to assign to the resource. If configured with a provider `default_tags` configuration block present, tags with matching keys will overwrite those defined at the provider-level.
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags` argument for the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to assign metadata in the form of key-value pairs to the delivery stream, enabling resource categorization, organization, and cost tracking. By configuring this argument, users can define tags for purposes such as identifying environments (e.g., "dev" or "prod"), managing billing, or applying governance policies, with the ability to override provider-level default tags if necessary.

arguments.name: tags_all
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags_all` argument for the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to define a comprehensive set of key-value tags inherited from both provider-level and resource-specific configurations. This enables consistent tagging for resource organization, cost allocation, and management across AWS services, aligning with common practices for tracking and categorizing cloud infrastructure.

arguments.name: version_id
arguments.llm_summary: The `version_id` argument for the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to specify the version of the source S3 object used for data delivery configuration. By setting this argument, users can control which specific version of an S3 object is referenced, enabling precise management of data sources and ensuring consistency in delivery stream behavior when working with versioned S3 buckets.

blocks.name: elasticsearch_configuration
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration options when `destination` is `elasticsearch`. See `elasticsearch_configuration` block below for details.

arguments.name: buffering_interval
arguments.description: (Optional) Buffer incoming data for the specified period of time, in seconds between 0 to 900, before delivering it to the destination. The default value is 300s.
arguments.llm_summary: The `buffering_interval` argument in the `elasticsearch_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to define the time, in seconds (0-900), that incoming data is buffered before being delivered to the Elasticsearch destination. Configuring this interval impacts data delivery latency and throughput, enabling users to balance real-time processing needs with efficient batching for optimized performance.

arguments.name: buffering_size
arguments.description: (Optional) Buffer incoming data to the specified size, in MBs between 1 to 100, before delivering it to the destination. The default value is 5MB.
arguments.llm_summary: The `buffering_size` argument in the `elasticsearch_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to define the maximum size (in MB, between 1 and 100) of incoming data that is buffered before being delivered to the Elasticsearch destination. Configuring this parameter impacts data delivery efficiency and latency, enabling users to optimize the trade-off between real-time processing and throughput for their streaming data pipeline.

arguments.name: cluster_endpoint
arguments.description: (Optional) The endpoint to use when communicating with the cluster. Conflicts with `domain_arn`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `cluster_endpoint` argument in the `elasticsearch_configuration` block of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to specify the direct endpoint for an Elasticsearch cluster to which delivery stream data will be sent. By setting this argument, users can control the communication path to a specific cluster, enabling precise data delivery without relying on a domain ARN. This is useful for scenarios where custom endpoints or non-standard configurations are required for Elasticsearch integration.

arguments.name: domain_arn
arguments.description: (Optional) The ARN of the Amazon ES domain. The pattern needs to be `arn:.*`. Conflicts with `cluster_endpoint`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `domain_arn` argument in the `elasticsearch_configuration` block of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to specify the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of an Amazon Elasticsearch Service (ES) domain to which Firehose will deliver data. By setting this argument, users can configure Firehose to integrate directly with a specific ES domain for real-time data indexing and analytics, enabling seamless delivery of streaming data to Elasticsearch. Note that this argument conflicts with `cluster_endpoint`, ensuring users define only one connection method.

arguments.name: index_name
arguments.description: (Required) The Elasticsearch index name.
arguments.llm_summary: The `index_name` argument in the `elasticsearch_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource specifies the name of the Elasticsearch index where data will be delivered and stored. By defining this required parameter, users control the target index for organizing and querying ingested data, aligning with common goals like structuring data for analytics or search functionality within Elasticsearch.

arguments.name: index_rotation_period
arguments.description: (Optional) The Elasticsearch index rotation period. Index rotation appends a timestamp to the IndexName to facilitate expiration of old data. Valid values are `NoRotation`, `OneHour`, `OneDay`, `OneWeek`, and `OneMonth`. The default value is `OneDay`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `index_rotation_period` argument in the `elasticsearch_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to define how frequently the Elasticsearch index is rotated by appending a timestamp to the index name. This configuration helps manage data retention and expiration by specifying rotation intervals such as `OneHour`, `OneDay`, or `OneMonth`, with a default of `OneDay`, aligning with common goals of optimizing data lifecycle and storage management.

arguments.name: retry_duration
arguments.description: (Optional) After an initial failure to deliver to Amazon Elasticsearch, the total amount of time, in seconds between 0 to 7200, during which Firehose re-attempts delivery (including the first attempt). After this time has elapsed, the failed documents are written to Amazon S3. The default value is 300s. There will be no retry if the value is 0.
arguments.llm_summary: The `retry_duration` argument in the `elasticsearch_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to define the maximum time, in seconds (0–7200), that Firehose will retry delivering data to Amazon Elasticsearch after an initial failure. By configuring this, users can control the retry behavior to balance delivery reliability and latency, ensuring failed documents are either successfully delivered within the specified timeframe or redirected to Amazon S3 for fallback storage.

arguments.name: role_arn
arguments.description: (Required) The ARN of the IAM role to be assumed by Firehose for calling the Amazon ES Configuration API and for indexing documents. The IAM role must have permission for `DescribeElasticsearchDomain`, `DescribeElasticsearchDomains`, and `DescribeElasticsearchDomainConfig`. The pattern needs to be `arn:.*`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `role_arn` argument specifies the IAM role that grants AWS Kinesis Firehose permissions to interact with the Amazon Elasticsearch Service (ES) API for domain configuration and document indexing. By defining this role, users enable Firehose to securely perform operations like describing Elasticsearch domains and indexing data, ensuring seamless integration with Elasticsearch for data delivery and processing.

arguments.name: s3_backup_mode
arguments.description: (Optional) Defines how documents should be delivered to Amazon S3. Valid values are `FailedDocumentsOnly` and `AllDocuments`. Default value is `FailedDocumentsOnly`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `s3_backup_mode` argument in the `elasticsearch_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to control how data is backed up to Amazon S3 when delivering documents to an Elasticsearch destination. It specifies whether only failed documents (`FailedDocumentsOnly`) or all documents (`AllDocuments`) are stored in S3, enabling users to configure backup behavior for data reliability and recovery purposes.

arguments.name: type_name
arguments.description: (Optional) The Elasticsearch type name with maximum length of 100 characters.
arguments.llm_summary: Defines the Elasticsearch type name for documents delivered to the target Elasticsearch cluster, allowing users to specify a logical grouping or classification for indexed data. This argument helps structure and organize data within Elasticsearch, aligning with user-defined schemas or application-specific requirements.

blocks.name: cloudwatch_logging_options
blocks.description: (Optional) The CloudWatch Logging Options for the delivery stream. See `cloudwatch_logging_options` block below for details.

arguments.name: enabled
arguments.description: (Optional) Enables or disables the logging. Defaults to `false`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `enabled` argument in the `cloudwatch_logging_options` block of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to control whether CloudWatch logging is activated for the delivery stream. Setting this argument to `true` enables logging of delivery stream activity, which is useful for monitoring, debugging, and auditing data flow operations, while leaving it as `false` (default) disables logging to reduce overhead or costs.

arguments.name: log_group_name
arguments.description: (Optional) The CloudWatch group name for logging. This value is required if `enabled` is true.
arguments.llm_summary: The `log_group_name` argument in the `cloudwatch_logging_options` block of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to specify the name of the CloudWatch Log Group where delivery stream logs will be stored. This enables detailed monitoring and troubleshooting of the delivery stream's operations, supporting common user goals like tracking data flow and diagnosing issues. It is required when logging is enabled (`enabled = true`).

arguments.name: log_stream_name
arguments.description: (Optional) The CloudWatch log stream name for logging. This value is required if `enabled` is true.
arguments.llm_summary: The `log_stream_name` argument in the `cloudwatch_logging_options` block of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to specify the name of the CloudWatch log stream where delivery stream activity logs will be sent. This enables detailed monitoring and troubleshooting by directing logs to a specific stream, and it is required when logging is enabled (`enabled = true`).

blocks.llm_summary: The `cloudwatch_logging_options` block within the `elasticsearch_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource enables detailed logging of delivery stream activities to Amazon CloudWatch Logs, providing visibility into data delivery operations and troubleshooting. It encapsulates settings for configuring log group and log stream details, helping users monitor and debug Elasticsearch delivery performance and issues effectively.

blocks.name: processing_configuration
blocks.description: (Optional) The data processing configuration.  See `processing_configuration` block below for details.

arguments.name: enabled
arguments.description: (Optional) Enables or disables data processing.
arguments.llm_summary: The `enabled` argument in the `processing_configuration` block of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to control whether data processing is activated for the delivery stream. Setting this to `true` enables the application of data transformation or enrichment logic (e.g., via AWS Lambda), while leaving it `false` bypasses processing, delivering raw data directly to the destination.

blocks.name: processors
blocks.description: (Optional) Specifies the data processors as multiple blocks. See `processors` block below for details.

arguments.name: type
arguments.description: (Required) The type of processor. Valid Values: `RecordDeAggregation`, `Lambda`, `MetadataExtraction`, `AppendDelimiterToRecord`, `Decompression`, `CloudWatchLogProcessing`. Validation is done against AWS SDK constants; so values not explicitly listed may also work.
arguments.llm_summary: The `type` argument specifies the kind of data transformation or processing to be applied to records in the delivery stream, enabling users to define how incoming data is handled before delivery. By setting this argument, users can configure processors such as `Lambda` for custom transformations, `MetadataExtraction` for parsing metadata, or `Decompression` for handling compressed data, aligning the stream's behavior with specific data processing requirements.

blocks.name: parameters
blocks.description: (Optional) Specifies the processor parameters as multiple blocks. See `parameters` block below for details.

arguments.name: parameter_name
arguments.description: (Required) Parameter name. Valid Values: `LambdaArn`, `NumberOfRetries`, `MetadataExtractionQuery`, `JsonParsingEngine`, `RoleArn`, `BufferSizeInMBs`, `BufferIntervalInSeconds`, `SubRecordType`, `Delimiter`, `CompressionFormat`, `DataMessageExtraction`. Validation is done against AWS SDK constants; so values not explicitly listed may also work.
arguments.llm_summary: The `parameter_name` argument specifies the name of a configuration parameter within the `parameters` block of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource, allowing users to define key operational settings for data delivery, transformation, or buffering. By setting this argument, users can control critical behaviors such as Lambda function integration (`LambdaArn`), retry policies (`NumberOfRetries`), data parsing (`JsonParsingEngine`), or compression formats (`CompressionFormat`), enabling tailored data processing and delivery workflows aligned with their specific use case.

arguments.name: parameter_value
arguments.description: (Required) Parameter value. Must be between 1 and 512 length (inclusive). When providing a Lambda ARN, you should specify the resource version as well. Parameters with default values, including NumberOfRetries(default: 3), RoleArn(default: firehose role ARN), BufferSizeInMBs(default: 1), and BufferIntervalInSeconds(default: 60), are not stored in terraform state. To prevent perpetual differences, it is therefore recommended to only include parameters with non-default values.
arguments.llm_summary: The `parameter_value` argument in the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to define the specific value for a configuration parameter within the delivery stream's `parameters` block. This argument is essential for customizing non-default behaviors, such as specifying a Lambda ARN with its resource version or overriding default values for retry counts, buffer size, or interval settings, enabling precise control over data processing and delivery functionality.

blocks.llm_summary: The `parameters` block within the `processors` configuration of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource defines key-value pairs that customize the behavior of data processing operations, such as transformations or validations, applied to incoming records. By configuring this block, users can fine-tune processor-specific settings to achieve precise control over how data is handled before delivery, enabling tailored processing workflows for their streaming use case.

The `processors` block within the `processing_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource defines and manages data transformation logic by specifying multiple data processors. This block enables users to preprocess or enrich incoming data before delivery, allowing for detailed control over data manipulation workflows such as format conversion, enrichment, or filtering to meet downstream requirements.

The `processing_configuration` block within the `elasticsearch_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource enables data transformation and preprocessing before delivery to Elasticsearch. It encapsulates settings for defining and managing data processors, such as AWS Lambda functions, to modify, filter, or enrich streaming data, allowing users to tailor data formats and content for optimized indexing and querying in Elasticsearch.

blocks.name: s3_configuration
blocks.description: (Required) The S3 Configuration. See `s3_configuration` block below for details.

arguments.name: bucket_arn
arguments.description: (Required) The ARN of the S3 bucket
arguments.llm_summary: The `bucket_arn` argument specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the S3 bucket where the Kinesis Firehose delivery stream will deliver data. By defining this required property, users configure the destination for data storage, enabling seamless integration with S3 for use cases like data archiving, analytics, or backup workflows.

arguments.name: buffering_interval
arguments.description: (Optional) Buffer incoming data for the specified period of time, in seconds, before delivering it to the destination. The default value is 300.
arguments.llm_summary: The `buffering_interval` argument in the `s3_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to define the time, in seconds, that incoming data is buffered before being delivered to the S3 destination. By configuring this parameter, users can optimize data delivery frequency to balance latency and throughput, aligning with use cases such as real-time analytics or batch processing.

arguments.name: buffering_size
arguments.description: (Optional) Buffer incoming data to the specified size, in MBs, before delivering it to the destination. The default value is 5. We recommend setting SizeInMBs to a value greater than the amount of data you typically ingest into the delivery stream in 10 seconds. For example, if you typically ingest data at 1 MB/sec set SizeInMBs to be 10 MB or higher.
arguments.llm_summary: The `buffering_size` argument in the `s3_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to define the size threshold (in MB) for buffering incoming data before it is delivered to the S3 destination. Configuring this value helps optimize delivery performance by batching data efficiently, with a recommended size greater than the typical data ingestion rate over a 10-second period to ensure smooth and cost-effective data transfer.

arguments.name: compression_format
arguments.description: (Optional) The compression format. If no value is specified, the default is `UNCOMPRESSED`. Other supported values are `GZIP`, `ZIP`, `Snappy`, & `HADOOP_SNAPPY`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `compression_format` argument in the `s3_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to specify the compression algorithm applied to data before it is delivered to the S3 bucket. Configuring this argument optimizes storage usage and reduces costs by compressing data in formats like `GZIP`, `ZIP`, `Snappy`, or `HADOOP_SNAPPY`, while leaving it `UNCOMPRESSED` by default if not specified.

arguments.name: error_output_prefix
arguments.description: (Optional) Prefix added to failed records before writing them to S3. Not currently supported for `redshift` destination. This prefix appears immediately following the bucket name. For information about how to specify this prefix, see Custom Prefixes for Amazon S3 Objects.
arguments.llm_summary: The `error_output_prefix` argument in the `s3_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to define a custom prefix for failed records written to the specified S3 bucket. This helps organize and identify error data by appending the prefix immediately after the bucket name, enabling easier troubleshooting and segregation of failed delivery attempts.

arguments.name: kms_key_arn
arguments.description: (Optional) Specifies the KMS key ARN the stream will use to encrypt data. If not set, no encryption will be used.
arguments.llm_summary: The `kms_key_arn` argument in the `s3_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to specify the ARN of a KMS key to enable server-side encryption for data delivered to the S3 destination. By setting this argument, users can enhance data security by encrypting the stream's contents at rest, aligning with compliance or organizational security requirements.

arguments.name: prefix
arguments.description: (Optional) The "YYYY/MM/DD/HH" time format prefix is automatically used for delivered S3 files. You can specify an extra prefix to be added in front of the time format prefix. Note that if the prefix ends with a slash, it appears as a folder in the S3 bucket
arguments.llm_summary: The `prefix` argument in the `s3_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to define a custom string that is prepended to the default "YYYY/MM/DD/HH" timestamp-based folder structure for S3 object delivery. By specifying this prefix, users can organize and categorize delivered files within the S3 bucket, enabling better data segmentation, logical grouping, or alignment with naming conventions, such as environment identifiers or application-specific folders.

arguments.name: role_arn
arguments.description: (Required) The ARN of the AWS credentials.
arguments.llm_summary: The `role_arn` argument specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that grants Kinesis Firehose permissions to access and deliver data to the configured S3 bucket. arguments.name: block_size_bytes
arguments.description: (Optional) The Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) block size. This is useful if you intend to copy the data from Amazon S3 to HDFS before querying. The default is 256 MiB and the minimum is 64 MiB. Kinesis Data Firehose uses this value for padding calculations.
arguments.llm_summary: The `block_size_bytes` argument in the `orc_ser_de` configuration of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to define the Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) block size for ORC serialization. arguments.name: bloom_filter_columns
arguments.description: (Optional) A list of column names for which you want Kinesis Data Firehose to create bloom filters.
arguments.llm_summary: The `bloom_filter_columns` argument allows users to specify a list of column names for which Kinesis Data Firehose will generate bloom filters when serializing data in ORC format. This enhances query performance and efficiency by enabling faster filtering of data during read operations, aligning with user goals of optimizing data processing and analytics workflows.

arguments.name: bloom_filter_false_positive_probability
arguments.description: (Optional) The Bloom filter false positive probability (FPP). The lower the FPP, the bigger the Bloom filter. The default value is `0.05`, the minimum is `0`, and the maximum is `1`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `bloom_filter_false_positive_probability` argument in the `orc_ser_de` configuration of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to control the accuracy of the Bloom filter used for ORC serialization. By specifying the false positive probability (FPP), users can balance memory usage and filter precision, with lower values improving accuracy at the cost of increased memory consumption. This is particularly useful for optimizing data processing and storage efficiency in scenarios where filtering accuracy impacts downstream analytics or query performance.

arguments.name: compression
arguments.description: (Optional) The compression code to use over data blocks. The default is `SNAPPY`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `compression` argument for the `orc_ser_de` configuration in the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to specify the compression algorithm applied to data blocks when serializing data in ORC (Optimized Row Columnar) format. By setting this argument, users can optimize storage efficiency and data transfer performance, with the default behavior using the `SNAPPY` compression method.

arguments.name: dictionary_key_threshold

arguments.llm_summary: The `dictionary_key_threshold` argument in the `orc_ser_de` configuration for the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to control the use of dictionary encoding for ORC serialization. By specifying a float value, users can optimize data compression and encoding behavior based on the fraction of non-null rows, enabling either more efficient storage or faster processing depending on the threshold set.

arguments.name: enable_padding
arguments.description: (Optional) Set this to `true` to indicate that you want stripes to be padded to the HDFS block boundaries. This is useful if you intend to copy the data from Amazon S3 to HDFS before querying. The default is `false`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `enable_padding` argument in the `orc_ser_de` configuration of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to control whether ORC file stripes are padded to align with HDFS block boundaries. Enabling this feature (`true`) is beneficial for workflows where data is later copied from Amazon S3 to HDFS for querying, ensuring optimal compatibility and performance during HDFS operations.

arguments.name: format_version
arguments.description: (Optional) The version of the file to write. The possible values are `V0_11` and `V0_12`. The default is `V0_12`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `format_version` argument for the `orc_ser_de` configuration in the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to specify the version of the ORC (Optimized Row Columnar) file format used for data serialization. By setting this argument to either `V0_11` or `V0_12` (default: `V0_12`), users can control compatibility and optimize data processing workflows for downstream analytics or storage systems that rely on specific ORC file versions.

arguments.name: padding_tolerance
arguments.description: (Optional) A float between 0 and 1 that defines the tolerance for block padding as a decimal fraction of stripe size. The default value is `0.05`, which means 5 percent of stripe size. For the default values of 64 MiB ORC stripes and 256 MiB HDFS blocks, the default block padding tolerance of 5 percent reserves a maximum of 3.2 MiB for padding within the 256 MiB block. In such a case, if the available size within the block is more than 3.2 MiB, a new, smaller stripe is inserted to fit within that space. This ensures that no stripe crosses block boundaries and causes remote reads within a node-local task. Kinesis Data Firehose ignores this parameter when `enable_padding` is `false`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `padding_tolerance` argument in the `orc_ser_de` configuration of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to define the block padding tolerance as a decimal fraction of the ORC stripe size, ensuring efficient data placement within HDFS blocks. By adjusting this value (default: 0.05), users can optimize stripe alignment to prevent remote reads and improve node-local task performance, but it is only relevant when `enable_padding` is set to `true`.

arguments.name: row_index_stride

arguments.llm_summary: The `row_index_stride` argument for the `orc_ser_de` configuration in the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to define the number of rows between index entries in ORC (Optimized Row Columnar) file serialization. Adjusting this value impacts query performance and file size, enabling users to optimize data retrieval efficiency versus storage overhead based on their specific analytics or processing needs.

arguments.name: stripe_size_bytes
arguments.description: (Optional) The number of bytes in each stripe. The default is 64 MiB and the minimum is 8 MiB.
arguments.llm_summary: "Configures the stripe size in bytes for ORC serialization within the Kinesis Firehose delivery stream, allowing users to optimize data storage and retrieval performance. By adjusting this value (default: 64 MiB, minimum: 8 MiB), users can balance memory usage and query efficiency based on their data processing needs."

arguments.name: enable_dictionary_compression
arguments.description: (Optional) Indicates whether to enable dictionary compression.
arguments.llm_summary: Controls whether dictionary compression is enabled for Parquet serialization in the Kinesis Firehose delivery stream, optimizing data storage by reducing file size. arguments.name: max_padding_bytes

arguments.llm_summary: The `log_group_name` argument in the `cloudwatch_logging_options` block of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to specify the name of the CloudWatch Log Group where delivery stream logs will be stored. This enables detailed monitoring and troubleshooting of the delivery stream's operations, supporting common user goals like tracking data flow and diagnosing issues. It is required when logging is enabled (`enabled = true`).

arguments.name: log_stream_name
arguments.description: (Optional) The CloudWatch log stream name for logging. This value is required if `enabled` is true.
arguments.llm_summary: The `log_stream_name` argument specifies the name of the CloudWatch log stream used for capturing and storing delivery stream logs when CloudWatch logging is enabled. Configuring this allows users to define the specific log stream for monitoring and troubleshooting the Kinesis Firehose delivery stream's operations, ensuring better observability and centralized log management.

blocks.llm_summary: The `cloudwatch_logging_options` block within the `s3_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource enables detailed logging of delivery stream activities to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. It encapsulates settings for configuring log group and log stream details, allowing users to monitor and troubleshoot data delivery to S3 with enhanced visibility and operational insights.

The `s3_configuration` block within the `iceberg_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource defines the settings for delivering data to an Amazon S3 bucket. It encapsulates configurations such as bucket details, access permissions, and optional features like compression, encryption, and buffering, enabling efficient and secure storage of streaming data. Configuring this block allows users to customize how data is stored in S3, ensuring compatibility with downstream analytics workflows, including Iceberg table formats.

The `iceberg_configuration` block within the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource defines settings specific to delivering data to an Apache Iceberg table when the `destination` is set to `iceberg`. It encapsulates configuration options for managing how data is formatted, partitioned, and stored in Iceberg-compatible formats, enabling users to seamlessly integrate Kinesis Firehose with Iceberg for efficient data lake management and analytics.

blocks.name: kinesis_source_configuration
blocks.description: (Optional) The stream and role Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) for a Kinesis data stream used as the source for a delivery stream. See `kinesis_source_configuration` block below for details.

arguments.name: kinesis_stream_arn
arguments.description: (Required) The kinesis stream used as the source of the firehose delivery stream.
arguments.llm_summary: The `kinesis_stream_arn` argument specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Kinesis data stream that serves as the source for the Firehose delivery stream, enabling the ingestion and processing of real-time data from the defined stream. By setting this required parameter, users establish the connection between the delivery stream and its data source, facilitating seamless data transfer for downstream storage or analytics workflows.

arguments.name: role_arn
arguments.description: (Required) The ARN of the role that provides access to the source Kinesis stream.
arguments.llm_summary: The `role_arn` argument specifies the IAM role that grants permissions for the delivery stream to access the source Kinesis stream in the `kinesis_source_configuration`. By defining this role, users enable the Firehose delivery stream to securely read data from the Kinesis stream, ensuring proper access control and integration between the two services.

blocks.llm_summary: The `kinesis_source_configuration` block in the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource defines the integration of a Kinesis data stream as the source for the delivery stream, specifying the stream's Amazon Resource Name (ARN) and the IAM role ARN required for access. This configuration enables users to seamlessly ingest and process real-time data from a Kinesis stream into the Firehose delivery pipeline, facilitating efficient data transformation and delivery to target destinations.

blocks.name: msk_source_configuration
blocks.description: (Optional) The configuration for the Amazon MSK cluster to be used as the source for a delivery stream. See `msk_source_configuration` block below for details.

arguments.name: msk_cluster_arn
arguments.description: (Required) The ARN of the Amazon MSK cluster.
arguments.llm_summary: The `msk_cluster_arn` argument specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Amazon MSK (Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka) cluster to be used as the data source for the Kinesis Firehose delivery stream. By setting this required value, users enable the delivery stream to ingest and process streaming data directly from the specified MSK cluster, facilitating seamless integration for real-time data pipelines and analytics workflows.

arguments.name: topic_name
arguments.description: (Required) The topic name within the Amazon MSK cluster.
arguments.llm_summary: Defines the specific Amazon MSK topic from which the Kinesis Firehose delivery stream will ingest data, enabling users to configure the source of streaming data for processing and delivery. Setting this argument ensures the delivery stream is linked to the correct topic within the MSK cluster, aligning with user goals of integrating managed Kafka data pipelines into downstream systems.

blocks.name: authentication_configuration
blocks.description: (Required) The authentication configuration of the Amazon MSK cluster. See `authentication_configuration` block below for details.

arguments.name: connectivity
arguments.description: (Required) The type of connectivity used to access the Amazon MSK cluster. Valid values: `PUBLIC`, `PRIVATE`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `connectivity` argument in the `authentication_configuration` block of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource specifies the network access type (`PUBLIC` or `PRIVATE`) used to connect to an Amazon MSK cluster. By defining this, users control whether the delivery stream communicates with the MSK cluster over public internet or private VPC networking, aligning with security and accessibility requirements for their infrastructure.

arguments.name: role_arn
arguments.description: (Required) The ARN of the role used to access the Amazon MSK cluster.
arguments.llm_summary: The `role_arn` argument specifies the IAM role's Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that grants the necessary permissions for the Kinesis Firehose delivery stream to authenticate and access the Amazon MSK cluster. Setting this value ensures secure integration with the MSK data source, enabling the delivery stream to read data from the cluster as part of its ingestion pipeline.

blocks.llm_summary: The `authentication_configuration` block within the `msk_source_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource defines the authentication mechanisms required to securely connect to an Amazon MSK cluster as a data source. It encapsulates settings related to credentials and security protocols, enabling users to establish authorized and encrypted communication for streaming data into the delivery stream. Configuring this block ensures secure integration with MSK, facilitating reliable and compliant data ingestion workflows.

The `msk_source_configuration` block in the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource configures the integration of an Amazon MSK (Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka) cluster as the data source for the delivery stream. It encapsulates settings required to define the connection and authentication details for the MSK cluster, enabling seamless ingestion of streaming data from Kafka topics into the delivery stream for further processing or storage.

blocks.name: opensearch_configuration
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration options when `destination` is `opensearch`. See `opensearch_configuration` block below for details.

arguments.name: buffering_interval
arguments.description: (Optional) Buffer incoming data for the specified period of time, in seconds between 0 to 900, before delivering it to the destination. The default value is 300s.
arguments.llm_summary: The `buffering_interval` argument in the `opensearch_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to define the time, in seconds (0-900), to buffer incoming data before delivering it to an OpenSearch destination. Configuring this interval impacts data delivery latency and throughput, enabling users to optimize for either faster delivery or more efficient batching based on their application's requirements.

arguments.name: buffering_size
arguments.description: (Optional) Buffer incoming data to the specified size, in MBs between 1 to 100, before delivering it to the destination. The default value is 5MB.
arguments.llm_summary: The `buffering_size` argument in the `opensearch_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to define the maximum size (in MB) of incoming data to buffer before delivering it to an OpenSearch destination. By configuring this parameter, users can optimize data delivery performance and control batching behavior, balancing throughput efficiency and latency to meet specific workload requirements.

arguments.name: cluster_endpoint
arguments.description: (Optional) The endpoint to use when communicating with the cluster. Conflicts with `domain_arn`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `cluster_endpoint` argument in the `opensearch_configuration` block of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to specify the OpenSearch cluster's endpoint for data delivery. By setting this argument, users define the communication target for streaming data into the cluster, enabling integration with a specific OpenSearch instance. This is typically used to configure direct connectivity to a cluster when the `domain_arn` is not provided.

arguments.name: domain_arn
arguments.description: (Optional) The ARN of the Amazon ES domain. The pattern needs to be `arn:.*`. Conflicts with `cluster_endpoint`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `domain_arn` argument in the `opensearch_configuration` block of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to specify the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of an OpenSearch (formerly Amazon Elasticsearch) domain to which Firehose will deliver data. By setting this argument, users can configure the delivery stream to integrate directly with a specific OpenSearch domain for indexing and search functionality, enabling seamless data ingestion into OpenSearch for analytics or querying purposes. Note that this argument conflicts with `cluster_endpoint`.

arguments.name: index_name
arguments.description: (Required) The OpenSearch index name.
arguments.llm_summary: The `index_name` argument in the `opensearch_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource specifies the name of the OpenSearch index where incoming data will be delivered and stored. By defining this required parameter, users control the target index for their streaming data, enabling structured organization and retrieval of records within their OpenSearch domain to support analytics, search, or monitoring workflows.

arguments.name: index_rotation_period
arguments.description: (Optional) The OpenSearch index rotation period. Index rotation appends a timestamp to the IndexName to facilitate expiration of old data. Valid values are `NoRotation`, `OneHour`, `OneDay`, `OneWeek`, and `OneMonth`. The default value is `OneDay`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `index_rotation_period` argument in the `opensearch_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to define the frequency at which OpenSearch indexes are rotated by appending a timestamp to the index name. This configuration helps manage data retention and expiration, enabling users to optimize storage and query performance by controlling how long data is retained in each index.

arguments.name: retry_duration
arguments.description: (Optional) After an initial failure to deliver to Amazon OpenSearch, the total amount of time, in seconds between 0 to 7200, during which Firehose re-attempts delivery (including the first attempt). After this time has elapsed, the failed documents are written to Amazon S3. The default value is 300s. There will be no retry if the value is 0.
arguments.llm_summary: The `retry_duration` argument in the `opensearch_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to define the maximum time, in seconds (0 to 7200), that Firehose will retry delivering data to Amazon OpenSearch after an initial failure. By configuring this, users can control the retry behavior to balance delivery reliability and latency, ensuring failed documents are either successfully delivered within the specified timeframe or redirected to Amazon S3 for fallback storage.

arguments.name: role_arn
arguments.description: (Required) The ARN of the IAM role to be assumed by Firehose for calling the Amazon ES Configuration API and for indexing documents. The IAM role must have permission for `DescribeDomain`, `DescribeDomains`, and `DescribeDomainConfig`. The pattern needs to be `arn:.*`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `role_arn` argument specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that Kinesis Firehose assumes to interact with the OpenSearch service (formerly Amazon Elasticsearch Service). By defining this role, users enable Firehose to perform essential operations like domain description and document indexing, ensuring seamless data delivery and integration with OpenSearch for analytics or search use cases.

arguments.name: s3_backup_mode
arguments.description: (Optional) Defines how documents should be delivered to Amazon S3. Valid values are `FailedDocumentsOnly` and `AllDocuments`. Default value is `FailedDocumentsOnly`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `s3_backup_mode` argument in the `opensearch_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to specify the behavior for backing up documents to Amazon S3. It controls whether only failed documents (`FailedDocumentsOnly`) or all documents (`AllDocuments`) are delivered to S3, enabling users to configure backup strategies for data reliability and recovery in OpenSearch integrations.

arguments.name: type_name
arguments.description: (Optional) The Elasticsearch type name with maximum length of 100 characters. Types are deprecated in OpenSearch_1.1. TypeName must be empty.
arguments.llm_summary: The `type_name` argument in the `opensearch_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to specify the Elasticsearch type name for indexing documents, with a maximum length of 100 characters. However, since types are deprecated in OpenSearch 1.1, this argument must be left empty, ensuring compatibility with modern OpenSearch versions and avoiding deprecated functionality.

blocks.name: cloudwatch_logging_options
blocks.description: (Optional) The CloudWatch Logging Options for the delivery stream. See `cloudwatch_logging_options` block below for details.

arguments.name: enabled
arguments.description: (Optional) Enables or disables the logging. Defaults to `false`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `enabled` argument in the `cloudwatch_logging_options` block of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to control whether CloudWatch logging is activated for the delivery stream. Setting this argument to `true` enables logging of delivery stream activity, which is useful for monitoring, debugging, and auditing data flow operations, while leaving it as `false` (default) disables logging to reduce overhead or costs.

arguments.name: log_group_name
arguments.description: (Optional) The CloudWatch group name for logging. This value is required if `enabled` is true.
arguments.llm_summary: The `log_group_name` argument in the `cloudwatch_logging_options` block of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to specify the name of the CloudWatch Log Group where delivery stream logs will be stored. Setting this argument enables detailed logging for monitoring and troubleshooting purposes, ensuring visibility into the delivery stream's operations when logging is enabled.

arguments.name: log_stream_name
arguments.description: (Optional) The CloudWatch log stream name for logging. This value is required if `enabled` is true.
arguments.llm_summary: The `log_stream_name` argument specifies the name of the CloudWatch log stream used for capturing and storing delivery stream logs when CloudWatch logging is enabled. Configuring this allows users to define the specific log stream for monitoring and troubleshooting the Kinesis Firehose delivery stream's operations, ensuring better observability and debugging capabilities.

blocks.llm_summary: The `cloudwatch_logging_options` block within the `opensearch_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource enables detailed logging of delivery stream activities to Amazon CloudWatch Logs, providing visibility into data delivery operations and troubleshooting. It encapsulates settings for configuring log group and log stream details, helping users monitor and debug the integration between Kinesis Firehose and OpenSearch effectively.

blocks.name: document_id_options
blocks.description: (Optional) The method for setting up document ID. See [`document_id_options` block] below for details.

arguments.name: default_document_id_format
arguments.description: (Required) The method for setting up document ID. Valid values: `FIREHOSE_DEFAULT`, `NO_DOCUMENT_ID`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `default_document_id_format` argument in the `document_id_options` block of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource specifies the method for assigning document IDs to records delivered to the destination. By setting this required string value to either `FIREHOSE_DEFAULT` or `NO_DOCUMENT_ID`, users control whether Firehose automatically generates unique document IDs (`FIREHOSE_DEFAULT`) or omits document IDs (`NO_DOCUMENT_ID`), impacting how records are identified and indexed in the target system.

blocks.llm_summary: The `document_id_options` block within the `opensearch_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource defines how document IDs are assigned when delivering data to Amazon OpenSearch Service. It encapsulates settings for customizing the method of document ID generation, enabling users to control data indexing behavior and ensure unique or consistent document identification in OpenSearch.

blocks.name: processing_configuration
blocks.description: (Optional) The data processing configuration. See `processing_configuration` block below for details.

arguments.name: enabled
arguments.description: (Optional) Enables or disables data processing.
arguments.llm_summary: The `enabled` argument in the `processing_configuration` block of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to control whether data processing is activated for the delivery stream. Setting this argument to `true` enables preprocessing functionality, such as data transformation or enrichment, which is commonly used to prepare data before delivery to the target destination.

blocks.name: processors
blocks.description: (Optional) Specifies the data processors as multiple blocks. See `processors` block below for details.

arguments.name: type
arguments.description: (Required) The type of processor. Valid Values: `RecordDeAggregation`, `Lambda`, `MetadataExtraction`, `AppendDelimiterToRecord`, `Decompression`, `CloudWatchLogProcessing`. Validation is done against AWS SDK constants; so values not explicitly listed may also work.
arguments.llm_summary: The `type` argument in the `processors` block of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource specifies the kind of data transformation or processing to be applied to records before delivery. By defining this argument, users can configure the behavior of the delivery stream to perform tasks such as deaggregating records, invoking Lambda functions, extracting metadata, appending delimiters, decompressing data, or processing CloudWatch logs, enabling tailored data handling to meet specific ingestion or transformation requirements.

blocks.name: parameters
blocks.description: (Optional) Specifies the processor parameters as multiple blocks. See `parameters` block below for details.

arguments.name: parameter_name
arguments.description: (Required) Parameter name. Valid Values: `LambdaArn`, `NumberOfRetries`, `MetadataExtractionQuery`, `JsonParsingEngine`, `RoleArn`, `BufferSizeInMBs`, `BufferIntervalInSeconds`, `SubRecordType`, `Delimiter`, `CompressionFormat`, `DataMessageExtraction`. Validation is done against AWS SDK constants; so values not explicitly listed may also work.
arguments.llm_summary: The `parameter_name` argument specifies the name of a configuration parameter within the `parameters` block of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource, enabling users to define key operational settings for data delivery and processing. By setting this argument, users can control behaviors such as retry policies, data transformation, buffering, compression, or metadata extraction, depending on the chosen parameter, aligning the delivery stream's functionality with specific application or infrastructure requirements.

arguments.name: parameter_value
arguments.description: (Required) Parameter value. Must be between 1 and 512 length (inclusive). When providing a Lambda ARN, you should specify the resource version as well. Parameters with default values, including NumberOfRetries(default: 3), RoleArn(default: firehose role ARN), BufferSizeInMBs(default: 1), and BufferIntervalInSeconds(default: 60), are not stored in terraform state. To prevent perpetual differences, it is therefore recommended to only include parameters with non-default values.
arguments.llm_summary: The `parameter_value` argument in the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to define the specific value for a configuration parameter within the delivery stream's `parameters` block. This value can control advanced behaviors such as Lambda function versions, retry counts, or buffer settings, enabling precise customization of data processing and delivery workflows. Users should specify non-default values to avoid state discrepancies and ensure consistent infrastructure behavior.

blocks.llm_summary: The `parameters` block within the `processors` configuration of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource defines key-value pairs that customize the behavior of data processing operations, such as transformations or validations, applied to incoming records. By configuring this block, users can fine-tune processor-specific settings to achieve precise control over how data is handled before delivery, enabling tailored processing workflows for their streaming data pipelines.

The `processors` block within the `processing_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource defines and manages data transformation logic by specifying multiple data processors. This block enables users to preprocess or enrich streaming data before delivery, allowing for detailed control over operations such as format conversion, data enrichment, or custom processing workflows to meet specific downstream requirements.

The `processing_configuration` block within the `opensearch_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource enables data transformation and preprocessing before delivery to OpenSearch. It encapsulates settings for defining and managing data processors, such as AWS Lambda functions, allowing users to customize, enrich, or format streaming data to meet specific indexing requirements or optimize OpenSearch ingestion workflows.

blocks.name: s3_configuration
blocks.description: (Required) The S3 Configuration. See `s3_configuration` block below for details.

arguments.name: bucket_arn
arguments.description: (Required) The ARN of the S3 bucket
arguments.llm_summary: The `bucket_arn` argument specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the S3 bucket where the Kinesis Firehose delivery stream will store its data. By defining this required property, users configure the destination for data delivery, enabling the stream to reliably transfer and persist records to the specified S3 bucket for further processing, storage, or analysis.

arguments.name: buffering_interval
arguments.description: (Optional) Buffer incoming data for the specified period of time, in seconds, before delivering it to the destination. The default value is 300.
arguments.llm_summary: The `buffering_interval` argument in the `s3_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to define the time, in seconds, that incoming data is buffered before being delivered to the S3 destination. By configuring this parameter, users can optimize data delivery frequency to balance latency and throughput, aligning with use cases such as real-time analytics or batch processing.

arguments.name: buffering_size
arguments.description: (Optional) Buffer incoming data to the specified size, in MBs, before delivering it to the destination. The default value is 5. We recommend setting SizeInMBs to a value greater than the amount of data you typically ingest into the delivery stream in 10 seconds. For example, if you typically ingest data at 1 MB/sec set SizeInMBs to be 10 MB or higher.
arguments.llm_summary: The `buffering_size` argument in the `s3_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource specifies the size threshold (in MB) for buffering incoming data before it is delivered to the S3 destination. Configuring this value allows users to optimize delivery performance by aligning the buffer size with their data ingestion rate, ensuring efficient batching and minimizing delivery latency.

arguments.name: compression_format
arguments.description: (Optional) The compression format. If no value is specified, the default is `UNCOMPRESSED`. Other supported values are `GZIP`, `ZIP`, `Snappy`, & `HADOOP_SNAPPY`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `compression_format` argument in the `s3_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to specify the compression algorithm applied to data before it is delivered to the S3 bucket. Configuring this argument optimizes storage usage and reduces costs by compressing data in formats like `GZIP`, `ZIP`, `Snappy`, or `HADOOP_SNAPPY`, while leaving it `UNCOMPRESSED` by default if not specified.

arguments.name: error_output_prefix
arguments.description: (Optional) Prefix added to failed records before writing them to S3. Not currently supported for `redshift` destination. This prefix appears immediately following the bucket name. For information about how to specify this prefix, see Custom Prefixes for Amazon S3 Objects.
arguments.llm_summary: The `error_output_prefix` argument in the `s3_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to define a custom prefix for failed records written to an S3 bucket, enabling organized error tracking and segregation of failed data. By specifying this prefix, users can streamline debugging and error management workflows by ensuring failed records are easily identifiable and stored with a consistent naming convention.

arguments.name: kms_key_arn
arguments.description: (Optional) Specifies the KMS key ARN the stream will use to encrypt data. If not set, no encryption will be used.
arguments.llm_summary: The `kms_key_arn` argument in the `s3_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to specify the ARN of a KMS key to enable server-side encryption for data delivered to the S3 destination. By setting this argument, users can enhance data security by encrypting the stream's payload at rest, aligning with compliance requirements or organizational security policies.

arguments.name: prefix
arguments.description: (Optional) The "YYYY/MM/DD/HH" time format prefix is automatically used for delivered S3 files. You can specify an extra prefix to be added in front of the time format prefix. Note that if the prefix ends with a slash, it appears as a folder in the S3 bucket
arguments.llm_summary: The `prefix` argument in the `s3_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to define a custom string that is prepended to the default "YYYY/MM/DD/HH" timestamp-based folder structure for S3 object delivery. This enables users to organize and categorize delivered files within the S3 bucket by adding an additional hierarchical layer, such as environment identifiers or application-specific tags, improving data organization and retrieval.

arguments.name: role_arn
arguments.description: (Required) The ARN of the AWS credentials.
arguments.llm_summary: The `role_arn` argument specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that grants Kinesis Firehose permissions to access and deliver data to the configured S3 bucket. By defining this required parameter, users ensure secure and authorized interactions between the delivery stream and the S3 destination, enabling seamless data transfer and storage in compliance with AWS access control policies.

blocks.name: cloudwatch_logging_options
blocks.description: (Optional) The CloudWatch Logging Options for the delivery stream. See `cloudwatch_logging_options` block below for details.

arguments.name: enabled
arguments.description: (Optional) Enables or disables the logging. Defaults to `false`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `enabled` argument in the `cloudwatch_logging_options` block of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to control whether CloudWatch logging is activated for the delivery stream. Setting this argument to `true` enables logging of delivery stream activity, which is useful for monitoring, debugging, and auditing data flow operations, while leaving it as `false` (default) disables logging to reduce overhead or costs.

arguments.name: log_group_name
arguments.description: (Optional) The CloudWatch group name for logging. This value is required if `enabled` is true.
arguments.llm_summary: The `log_group_name` argument in the `cloudwatch_logging_options` block of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to specify the name of the CloudWatch Log Group where delivery stream logs will be stored. Setting this argument enables detailed logging for monitoring and troubleshooting, aligning with user goals of tracking delivery stream activity and ensuring operational visibility when logging is enabled.

arguments.name: log_stream_name
arguments.description: (Optional) The CloudWatch log stream name for logging. This value is required if `enabled` is true.
arguments.llm_summary: The `log_stream_name` argument in the `cloudwatch_logging_options` block of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to specify the name of the CloudWatch log stream where delivery stream activity logs will be sent. This configuration is essential for enabling detailed logging when `enabled` is set to true, helping users monitor and troubleshoot data delivery operations effectively.

blocks.llm_summary: The `cloudwatch_logging_options` block within the `s3_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource enables detailed logging of delivery stream activities to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. It encapsulates settings for configuring log group and log stream details, allowing users to monitor and troubleshoot data delivery to S3 with enhanced visibility and operational insights.

The `s3_configuration` block within the `opensearch_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource defines the integration with Amazon S3 for storing and buffering data before delivery to OpenSearch. It encapsulates settings related to S3 bucket details, access permissions, compression, encryption, and error handling, enabling users to manage data durability, security, and preprocessing. Configuring this block ensures reliable intermediate storage and optimized data flow for OpenSearch ingestion.

blocks.name: vpc_config
blocks.description: (Optional) The VPC configuration for the delivery stream to connect to OpenSearch associated with the VPC. See `vpc_config` block below for details.

arguments.name: role_arn
arguments.description: (Required) The ARN of the IAM role to be assumed by Firehose for calling the Amazon EC2 configuration API and for creating network interfaces. Make sure role has necessary IAM permissions
arguments.llm_summary: The `role_arn` argument specifies the IAM role that Amazon Kinesis Firehose assumes to access the Amazon EC2 configuration API and create network interfaces within a VPC. By setting this required value, users enable Firehose to securely integrate with VPC resources, ensuring proper permissions for network operations and data delivery.

arguments.name: security_group_ids
arguments.description: (Required) A list of security group IDs to associate with Kinesis Firehose.
arguments.llm_summary: The `security_group_ids` argument in the `vpc_config` block of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource specifies the set of security groups to associate with the delivery stream's VPC endpoint, controlling inbound and outbound network traffic. By defining this argument, users ensure secure communication between the delivery stream and other resources within the VPC, aligning with common goals like enforcing network access policies and isolating traffic for compliance or security purposes.

arguments.name: subnet_ids
arguments.description: (Required) A list of subnet IDs to associate with Kinesis Firehose.
arguments.llm_summary: The `subnet_ids` argument in the `vpc_config` block of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource specifies the set of subnet IDs within a VPC where the delivery stream can operate. This configuration ensures the Firehose delivery stream can securely access resources or endpoints within the specified subnets, enabling private network communication and integration with services like Amazon S3 or Redshift in a controlled VPC environment.

arguments.name: vpc_id
arguments.llm_summary: The `vpc_id` argument in the `vpc_config` block of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to specify the ID of the VPC where the delivery stream's network resources will operate. arguments.llm_summary: The `buffering_size` argument in the `s3_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to define the maximum size (in MB) of incoming data to buffer before delivering it to the S3 destination. arguments.name: bucket_arn
arguments.description: (Required) The ARN of the S3 bucket
arguments.llm_summary: The `bucket_arn` argument specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the S3 bucket where the Kinesis Firehose delivery stream will deliver data. By defining this required property, users configure the destination for data storage, enabling seamless integration with S3 for use cases like data archiving, analytics, or further processing.

arguments.name: buffering_interval
arguments.description: (Optional) Buffer incoming data for the specified period of time, in seconds, before delivering it to the destination. The default value is 300.
arguments.llm_summary: The `buffering_interval` argument in the `s3_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource specifies the time, in seconds, to buffer incoming data before delivering it to the S3 destination. This allows users to control the trade-off between delivery frequency and data batching efficiency, optimizing for either lower latency or reduced storage and processing costs.

arguments.name: buffering_size
arguments.description: (Optional) Buffer incoming data to the specified size, in MBs, before delivering it to the destination. The default value is 5. We recommend setting SizeInMBs to a value greater than the amount of data you typically ingest into the delivery stream in 10 seconds. For example, if you typically ingest data at 1 MB/sec set SizeInMBs to be 10 MB or higher.
arguments.llm_summary: The `buffering_size` argument in the `s3_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to define the maximum size (in MB) of incoming data to buffer before delivering it to the S3 destination. Configuring this parameter impacts data delivery efficiency by optimizing batch size for ingestion rates, ensuring smoother throughput and reducing the frequency of delivery operations, which is particularly useful for high-volume or time-sensitive data streams.

arguments.name: compression_format
arguments.description: (Optional) The compression format. If no value is specified, the default is `UNCOMPRESSED`. Other supported values are `GZIP`, `ZIP`, `Snappy`, & `HADOOP_SNAPPY`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `compression_format` argument in the `s3_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to specify the compression algorithm applied to data before it is delivered to the S3 bucket. Configuring this argument optimizes storage usage and potentially improves data transfer efficiency, supporting common goals like cost reduction and performance optimization for large-scale data ingestion workflows.

arguments.name: error_output_prefix
arguments.description: (Optional) Prefix added to failed records before writing them to S3. Not currently supported for `redshift` destination. This prefix appears immediately following the bucket name. For information about how to specify this prefix, see Custom Prefixes for Amazon S3 Objects.
arguments.llm_summary: The `error_output_prefix` argument in the `s3_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to define a custom prefix for failed records written to an S3 bucket, enabling better organization and identification of error data. By specifying this prefix, users can streamline error tracking and debugging workflows, ensuring failed records are easily distinguishable from other data in the bucket.

arguments.name: kms_key_arn
arguments.description: (Optional) Specifies the KMS key ARN the stream will use to encrypt data. If not set, no encryption will be used.
arguments.llm_summary: The `kms_key_arn` argument in the `s3_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to specify the ARN of a KMS key to enable server-side encryption for data delivered to the S3 destination. By setting this argument, users can enhance data security by encrypting the stream's payload at rest, aligning with compliance requirements or organizational security policies.

arguments.name: prefix
arguments.description: (Optional) The "YYYY/MM/DD/HH" time format prefix is automatically used for delivered S3 files. You can specify an extra prefix to be added in front of the time format prefix. Note that if the prefix ends with a slash, it appears as a folder in the S3 bucket
arguments.llm_summary: The `prefix` argument in the `s3_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to define a custom string that is prepended to the default "YYYY/MM/DD/HH" timestamp-based folder structure for delivered S3 files. This enables users to organize and categorize data in S3 buckets by adding an additional hierarchical layer, such as environment or application-specific prefixes, with the option to create folder-like structures if the prefix ends with a slash.
