arguments.llm_summary: The `parameter_value` argument in the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to define the specific value for a configuration parameter within the delivery stream's `parameters` block. This value can control advanced behaviors such as retry settings, buffer configurations, or Lambda function versions, enabling users to customize the stream's operational characteristics. It is particularly useful for overriding default values to meet specific requirements, ensuring precise control over delivery stream functionality.

blocks.llm_summary: The `parameters` block within the `processors` configuration of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource defines key-value pairs that customize the behavior of data transformation or enrichment processors. This block enables fine-grained control over processor-specific settings, such as parameter names, values, and data handling options, allowing users to tailor processing logic to meet specific data delivery or transformation requirements.

The `processors` block within the `processing_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource defines and manages data transformation logic by specifying multiple data processors. This block enables users to preprocess or enrich incoming data before delivery, allowing for detailed control over data manipulation workflows such as format conversion, enrichment, or filtering to meet downstream requirements.

The `processing_configuration` block within the `splunk_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource enables data transformation and enrichment before delivery to Splunk. It encapsulates settings for enabling and managing data processors, such as AWS Lambda functions, allowing users to preprocess, filter, or modify streaming data to meet specific requirements or optimize ingestion workflows. Configuring this block ensures greater control over data formatting and quality, aligning the delivery stream with Splunk's ingestion needs.

blocks.name: s3_configuration
blocks.description: (Required) The S3 Configuration. See `s3_configuration` block below for details.

arguments.name: bucket_arn
arguments.description: (Required) The ARN of the S3 bucket
arguments.llm_summary: The `bucket_arn` argument specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the S3 bucket where the Kinesis Firehose delivery stream will deliver data. By defining this required property, users configure the destination for data storage, enabling seamless integration with S3 for use cases like data archiving, analytics, or backup workflows.

arguments.name: buffering_interval
arguments.description: (Optional) Buffer incoming data for the specified period of time, in seconds, before delivering it to the destination. The default value is 300.
arguments.llm_summary: The `buffering_interval` argument in the `s3_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource specifies the time, in seconds, to buffer incoming data before delivering it to the S3 destination. This allows users to control the delivery frequency, balancing lower latency with higher efficiency by batching data over the defined interval (default: 300 seconds).

arguments.name: buffering_size
arguments.description: (Optional) Buffer incoming data to the specified size, in MBs, before delivering it to the destination. The default value is 5. We recommend setting SizeInMBs to a value greater than the amount of data you typically ingest into the delivery stream in 10 seconds. For example, if you typically ingest data at 1 MB/sec set SizeInMBs to be 10 MB or higher.
arguments.llm_summary: The `buffering_size` argument in the `s3_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to define the maximum size (in MB) of incoming data that is buffered before being delivered to the S3 destination. Configuring this parameter impacts data delivery efficiency and latency, enabling users to optimize throughput based on their ingestion rate and delivery stream performance requirements.

arguments.name: compression_format
arguments.description: (Optional) The compression format. If no value is specified, the default is `UNCOMPRESSED`. Other supported values are `GZIP`, `ZIP`, `Snappy`, & `HADOOP_SNAPPY`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `compression_format` argument in the `s3_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to specify the compression algorithm applied to data before it is delivered to the S3 bucket. Configuring this argument optimizes storage usage and improves data transfer efficiency, supporting formats like `GZIP`, `ZIP`, `Snappy`, and `HADOOP_SNAPPY`, or leaving data uncompressed by default (`UNCOMPRESSED`).

arguments.name: error_output_prefix
arguments.description: (Optional) Prefix added to failed records before writing them to S3. Not currently supported for `redshift` destination. This prefix appears immediately following the bucket name. For information about how to specify this prefix, see Custom Prefixes for Amazon S3 Objects.
arguments.llm_summary: The `error_output_prefix` argument in the `s3_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to define a custom prefix for failed records written to an S3 bucket. This configuration helps organize and identify error logs by appending the specified prefix immediately after the bucket name, enabling streamlined debugging and error tracking for delivery failures.

arguments.name: kms_key_arn
arguments.description: (Optional) Specifies the KMS key ARN the stream will use to encrypt data. If not set, no encryption will be used.
arguments.llm_summary: The `kms_key_arn` argument in the `s3_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to specify the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of a KMS key to enable server-side encryption for data delivered to the S3 destination. By setting this argument, users can enhance data security by encrypting the stream's payload at rest, aligning with compliance requirements or organizational security policies.

arguments.name: prefix
arguments.description: (Optional) The "YYYY/MM/DD/HH" time format prefix is automatically used for delivered S3 files. You can specify an extra prefix to be added in front of the time format prefix. Note that if the prefix ends with a slash, it appears as a folder in the S3 bucket
arguments.llm_summary: The `prefix` argument in the `s3_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to define a custom string that is prepended to the default "YYYY/MM/DD/HH" timestamp-based folder structure for S3 object delivery. This enables users to organize and categorize delivered data within the S3 bucket by adding an additional hierarchical layer, such as environment identifiers or application-specific tags, improving data management and retrieval.

arguments.name: role_arn
arguments.description: (Required) The ARN of the AWS credentials.
arguments.llm_summary: The `role_arn` argument specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that grants Kinesis Firehose permissions to access and deliver data to the configured S3 bucket. By defining this required parameter, users ensure secure and authorized interactions between the delivery stream and the S3 destination, enabling seamless data transfer and storage in compliance with AWS access control policies.

blocks.name: cloudwatch_logging_options
blocks.description: (Optional) The CloudWatch Logging Options for the delivery stream. See `cloudwatch_logging_options` block below for details.

arguments.name: enabled
arguments.description: (Optional) Enables or disables the logging. Defaults to `false`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `enabled` argument in the `cloudwatch_logging_options` block of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to control whether CloudWatch logging is activated for the delivery stream. Setting this argument to `true` enables logging of delivery stream activity, which is useful for monitoring, debugging, and auditing data flow operations, while leaving it as `false` (default) disables logging to reduce overhead or costs.

arguments.name: log_group_name
arguments.description: (Optional) The CloudWatch group name for logging. This value is required if `enabled` is true.
arguments.llm_summary: The `log_group_name` argument in the `cloudwatch_logging_options` block of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to specify the name of the CloudWatch Log Group where delivery stream logs will be stored. Setting this argument enables detailed logging for monitoring and troubleshooting data delivery operations, aligning with user goals of enhancing observability and operational insights.

arguments.name: log_stream_name
arguments.description: (Optional) The CloudWatch log stream name for logging. This value is required if `enabled` is true.
arguments.llm_summary: The `log_stream_name` argument in the `cloudwatch_logging_options` block of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to specify the name of the CloudWatch log stream where delivery stream activity logs will be sent. This configuration is essential for enabling detailed logging when `enabled` is set to true, helping users monitor and troubleshoot data delivery operations effectively.

blocks.llm_summary: The `cloudwatch_logging_options` block within the `s3_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource enables detailed logging of delivery stream activities to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. It encapsulates settings for configuring log group and log stream details, allowing users to monitor and troubleshoot data delivery to S3 with enhanced visibility and operational insights.

The `s3_configuration` block within the `splunk_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource defines the integration with an Amazon S3 bucket, enabling the delivery stream to store data in S3 as part of its processing pipeline. This block encapsulates settings related to S3 bucket details, data buffering, compression, encryption, and error handling, providing users with fine-grained control over how data is staged or archived before being forwarded to Splunk. Configuring this block ensures reliable data storage and enhances fault tolerance in the event of delivery failures to Splunk.

blocks.name: secrets_manager_configuration

arguments.name: enabled
arguments.description: (Optional) Enables or disables the Secrets Manager configuration.
arguments.llm_summary: The `enabled` argument in the `secrets_manager_configuration` block of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to control whether integration with AWS Secrets Manager is active. Setting this to `true` enables the use of Secrets Manager for securely managing and retrieving sensitive credentials (e.g., database or API keys) required by the delivery stream, aligning with common goals of enhancing security and simplifying secret management.

arguments.name: role_arn
arguments.description: (Optional) The ARN of the role the stream assumes.
arguments.llm_summary: The `role_arn` argument in the `secrets_manager_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource specifies the IAM role that the delivery stream assumes to securely access and retrieve secrets from AWS Secrets Manager. Configuring this argument enables the stream to authenticate and manage permissions for accessing sensitive data, ensuring secure integration with Secrets Manager for encryption or other secret-related operations.

arguments.name: secret_arn
arguments.description: (Optional) The ARN of the Secrets Manager secret. This value is required if `enabled` is true.
arguments.llm_summary: The `secret_arn` argument in the `secrets_manager_configuration` block of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of a Secrets Manager secret, enabling secure access to sensitive credentials or configuration data for the delivery stream. This argument is required when `enabled` is set to true, allowing users to integrate Secrets Manager for managing authentication or other sensitive parameters, typically to enhance security and streamline secret management within the delivery stream's operations.

blocks.llm_summary: The `secrets_manager_configuration` block within the `splunk_configuration` of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource specifies the integration with AWS Secrets Manager to securely manage and retrieve authentication credentials for delivering data to Splunk. This block encapsulates settings related to the use of Secrets Manager, such as the secret ARN and role ARN, enabling users to securely configure and automate credential management for Splunk delivery streams without hardcoding sensitive information.

The `splunk_configuration` block in the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource defines settings for delivering streaming data to a Splunk endpoint, enabling seamless integration with Splunk for real-time data ingestion and analysis. It encapsulates configuration options specific to Splunk as the destination, allowing users to customize delivery parameters and optimize data flow for logging, monitoring, or analytics use cases.

blocks.name: timeouts

arguments.name: create
arguments.llm_summary: The `create` argument within the `timeouts` block of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to specify the maximum duration (as a string, e.g., "10m" for 10 minutes) Terraform should wait for the delivery stream to be successfully created. Configuring this timeout helps manage deployment expectations and avoid prolonged waits or premature failures during resource provisioning.

arguments.name: delete
arguments.llm_summary: The `delete` argument within the `timeouts` block of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to specify the maximum duration (as a string) Terraform will wait for the delivery stream to be deleted during resource destruction. Configuring this timeout ensures predictable behavior during the resource lifecycle, particularly for managing cleanup operations in environments with complex dependencies or long deletion processes.

arguments.name: update
arguments.llm_summary: The `update` argument within the `timeouts` block of the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource allows users to specify the maximum duration (as a string, e.g., "30m") Terraform will wait for updates to the delivery stream to complete. Configuring this timeout helps manage long-running update operations, ensuring Terraform does not prematurely fail during resource modifications.

blocks.llm_summary: The `timeouts` configuration block in the `aws_kinesis_firehose_delivery_stream` resource defines the maximum duration allowed for specific operations, such as creating, updating, or deleting the delivery stream. By configuring this block, users can manage operation time limits to ensure predictable behavior and avoid prolonged execution during resource lifecycle changes, enhancing control over deployment and infrastructure stability.
